source.name: Pressing Tab in an open date field must move focus to the next form field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/mymth/vanillajs-datepicker/issues/156) at 6156648a4cbcb662d4e1f5f4b449adf0f9a67759. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1533350d5ea7d790ea36fcdaf4bcbfd170ddcfab; routing auto.

journey.title: Tab out of the visit date into the access notes
journey.goal: Pressing Tab in the open date field moves focus to the next form field so the user can keep typing

functionalJourney.title: Pick a visit date with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day in the calendar fills the visit date field

guards.title: Pick the next day with arrow keys
guards.goal: Arrow keys move the calendar focus and Enter commits the date

plan.root_cause: The datepicker popup does not close when the Tab key is pressed, causing focus to remain trapped or lost, preventing movement to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the datepicker input that hides the popup when the Tab key is pressed and the popup is active, then proceeds with the original keydown handling.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the datepicker popup is open will close the popup and move focus to the next form field, allowing keyboard users to navigate away from the datepicker.
functional_risks: Hiding the datepicker on Tab might interfere with users who want to navigate within the popup using Tab (if the popup had focusable elements). However, the current popup does not have visible focusable elements, so this risk is low.
The original onKeydown handler might rely on the event not being altered; we are calling it after potentially hiding the picker, which could affect its behavior if it checks the active state.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab in the visit-date field when the datepicker is open moves focus to the notes field.
Verify that pressing Tab in the visit-date field when the datepicker is closed moves focus to the notes field (existing behavior).
Verify that other keys (like ArrowDown, Escape, etc.) in the datepicker input still work as expected.
Verify that clicking on the datepicker input to open it and then clicking outside still closes it.
Verify that the datepicker still functions correctly for mouse and touch users.
